subtitle: When Silver Fell Silent: Chandragupta II and the Last of the Saka Satraps

panels.shot: split composition, half showing a fading satrap coin over a coastal port, half a rising Gupta emperor over new silver
panels.action: On one side, Rudrasimha III stands in worn armor before a hazy western port; on the other, Chandragupta II in gleaming regalia holds a freshly struck silver coin, the sea and ships behind him under a reddening sky.

dialogue.text: For nearly four hundred years the Saka satraps ruled the western seas, until Chandragupta II took their mints, their ports, and their place—leaving only silent coins to tell how an age ended.

i18n.hi: करीब चार सौ साल शाक क्षत्रपों ने पश्चिमी समुद्र पर राज किया, जब तक चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय ने उनके टकसाल, बंदरगाह और गद्दी छीनकर, बस खामोश सिक्के छोड़ दिए कि वे कहानी कहें कि एक युग कैसे खत्म हुआ।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of an ancient silver coin spinning in mid-air
panels.action: An old Western Kshatrapa silver coin spins above a stone floor, its Saka legend and standing king glinting, as dust motes hang in the air of a dim treasury.

dialogue.text: Long before Chandragupta II, Saka satraps stamped silver at western ports, their coins ringing from Bharuch to distant seas.

i18n.hi: चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय से बहुत पहले, शाक क्षत्रप पश्चिमी बंदरगाहों पर चांदी ढालते थे, उनके सिक्कों की टनटन भरुच से दूर समंदरों तक सुनाई देती थी।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the western coast showing ports and inland routes
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Gujarat coast shows the harbor of Bharuch with masts and cargo, caravans snaking inland toward Malwa’s plateau, smoke rising from busy towns.

dialogue.text: These coins carried more than metal. They tied Malwa’s uplands to Gujarat’s harbours and to the wider trade of the Indian Ocean.

i18n.hi: ये सिक्के सिर्फ धातु नहीं ढोते थे। वे मालवा के पठारों को गुजरात के बंदरगाहों और हिंद महासागर की बड़ी मंडियों से जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: mirrored medium shot, both rulers in profile facing opposite directions
panels.action: Rudrasimha III stands in profile, cloaked in the older Saka style, eyes shadowed; opposite him, Chandragupta II in Gupta court attire, diademed, calm and calculating, the two separated by an invisible divide.

dialogue.text: By the late fourth century, Rudrasimha III held the last Kshatrapa throne, as Chandragupta II rose in the east, his gaze turning steadily toward the western sea.

i18n.hi: चौथी सदी के अंत तक, रुद्रसिंह तृतीय आख़िरी क्षत्रप सिंहासन पर था, और पूरब में चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय उठ रहा था, जिसकी नज़र धीरे‑धीरे पश्चिमी समुद्र पर टिक रही थी।

panels.shot: interior court wide shot contrasting two thrones side by side in split-scene
panels.action: In a split-scene, Rudrasimha III sits in a modest court with worn pillars and anxious courtiers, while Chandragupta II presides over a bright Gupta hall, attendants presenting maps and revenue records.

dialogue.text: The Gupta realm was expanding, its revenues swelling. The old satrap domain, rich in ports and silver, now stood as a tempting, vulnerable neighbour.

i18n.hi: गुप्त साम्राज्य फैल रहा था, खजाने भर रहे थे। पुराने क्षत्रप प्रदेश, बंदरगाहों और चांदी से भरपूर, अब लालच जगाते, असुरक्षित पड़ोसी बन गए थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Chandragupta II and his minister studying an inscription slab map
panels.action: Chandragupta II leans over a stone slab etched with a rough map of Malwa and Gujarat, while a minister indicates Udayagiri and the western regions with a stylus.

dialogue.text: Around 401 CE, his minister Virasena recorded at Udayagiri that the emperor ‘conquered the whole of the western region.’ The inscription is brief, but its shadow is long.

i18n.hi: लगभग 401 ईस्वी में, उसके मंत्री वीरसेन ने उदयगिरि पर लिखा कि सम्राट ने ‘पूरा पश्चिम जीता’। लेख छोटा है, पर उसकी छाया दूर तक जाती है।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Udayagiri hill with royal entourage
panels.action: Chandragupta II stands before the rock-cut slopes of Udayagiri, banners fluttering, brahmins, soldiers and artisans around him, as masons chip at the cliff to shape a sanctuary.

dialogue.text: At Udayagiri near Vidisha, the hill echoed with chisels and chants as Gupta power marked the stone, even as plans for the western march took shape.

i18n.hi: विदिशा के पास उदयगिरि पर पहाड़ी छैनी और मंत्रों से गूंज उठी, जब गुप्त शक्ति ने पत्थर पर अपनी छाप छोड़ी, और साथ‑साथ पश्चिम की चढ़ाई के नक्शे बने।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandragupta II in war council over campaign map
panels.action: In a tent lit by oil lamps, Chandragupta II stands over a cloth map marked with pebbles for towns like Ujjain and Bharuch, while commanders in armour listen in tense silence.

dialogue.text: “Malwa, then the coast. Guard the routes, spare the merchants,” Chandragupta II says.

i18n.hi: "पहले मालवा, फिर तट। राहें संभालो, व्यापारियों को मत छूना," चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय कहता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of two armies facing each other on a dusty plain, but with no combat shown
panels.action: On a hazy plain, the Gupta host and Western Kshatrapa forces stand arrayed at a distance, banners snapping in the wind, elephants and cavalry poised yet unmoving as the sky darkens.

dialogue.text: The chronicles are silent on the battles. We know only that Gupta power pressed westward, and the satrap forces could not finally hold.

i18n.hi: इतिहास चुप है कि लड़ाइयाँ कैसी थीं। बस इतना दिखता है कि गुप्त ताकत पश्चिम की ओर धकेलती गई, और क्षत्रप सेना आख़िर थाम न सकी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Rudrasimha III in his mint, watching coins being struck
panels.action: Rudrasimha III stands within a mint-house as workers hammer silver blanks, his face lined, eyes following each coin as if counting not money, but remaining days of his rule.

dialogue.text: Rudrasimha III continued to issue silver, his name and title in Saka letters. But his line would be the last to do so.

i18n.hi: रुद्रसिंह तृतीय चांदी के सिक्के ढालता रहा, उसका नाम और उपाधि शाक लिपि में। पर उसकी ही पंक्ति आख़िरी रहने वाली थी।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of two coins side by side, one satrap, one Gupta western-style
panels.action: On a trader’s palm, an older Western Kshatrapa coin showing a standing king lies beside a newer Gupta silver piece copying the same form, but bearing Chandragupta II’s name.

dialogue.text: Then the pattern changes. The Kshatrapa coins of Rudrasimha III cease, and new silver appears—Gupta, yet struck in the old western style.

i18n.hi: फिर ढंग बदल जाता है। रुद्रसिंह तृतीय के क्षत्रप सिक्के थम जाते हैं, और नई चांदी उभरती है—गुप्त, पर ढलाई वही पुरानी पश्चिमी अदा में।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandragupta II inspecting newly struck western-style coins
panels.action: Chandragupta II stands in a coastal mint, an official kneeling as he offers a tray of freshly struck western-style silver coins, the emperor studying their familiar yet now Gupta-inscribed design.

dialogue.text: “Let their traders see a known face, and read a new name,” he murmurs.

i18n.hi: "उनके सौदागर वही चेहरा देखें, पर नया नाम पढ़ें," वह धीमे से कहता है।

panels.shot: aerial view of Bharuch harbour now under Gupta banners
panels.action: An elevated view over Bharuch shows ships moored at crowded quays, cranes lifting goods, while Gupta banners flutter from warehouses and a small fort above the harbour.

dialogue.text: Control of Malwa and Gujarat brought Bharuch’s harbour into Gupta hands, its customs, tolls and sea-routes now feeding a north Indian court far from the surf.

i18n.hi: मालवा और गुजरात पर पकड़ ने भरुच का बंदरगाह गुप्त हाथों में दे दिया, उसके महसूल, चुंगी और समुंदर‑रास्ते अब दूर उत्तर के दरबार को समुद्री लहरों से जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of merchants exchanging Gupta western-style coins in a market
panels.action: In a bustling coastal bazaar, Indian, foreign and local merchants weigh and exchange the new Gupta silver coins, their scales balanced over piles of spices and textiles.

dialogue.text: Merchants in the western markets now counted Gupta coins, their trust eased by the familiar shape, their allegiance gently redirected by the altered legend.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी मंडियों के सौदागर अब गुप्त सिक्के गिनते थे, पहचानी आकृति से भरोसा बना रहता, और बदले हुए लेख से उनकी निष्ठा धीरे‑धीरे नई तरफ मुड़ती।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of a silent, abandoned satrap mint
panels.action: Inside an abandoned mint, broken dies lie scattered, furnaces cold, cobwebs draped over unused anvils, a single forgotten Kshatrapa coin resting in a crack of the stone floor.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists and numismatists, centuries later, would notice what contemporaries heard as a faint stop: the western satrap mints fell silent.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद पुरातत्त्ववेत्ता और मुद्रा‑विशेषज्ञों ने वह बात पकड़ी जो समकालीनों ने बस हल्की खामोशी की तरह सुनी थी: पश्चिमी क्षत्रप टकसालें थम गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern scholar’s hand holding Rudrasimha III’s coin with reflection of Chandragupta II statue in glass
panels.action: A modern scholar’s hand holds a worn coin of Rudrasimha III under glass, where the faint reflection of a museum statue of Chandragupta II overlaps the tiny portrait.

dialogue.text: From Rapson’s catalogues to later histories, the last coins of Rudrasimha III mark the vanishing of the Western Kshatrapas and the rise of Gupta control over the western sea.

i18n.hi: रैप्सन की सूचियों से लेकर बाद की किताबों तक, रुद्रसिंह तृतीय के आख़िरी सिक्के दिखाते हैं जहाँ पश्चिमी क्षत्रप मिटते हैं और गुप्तों की पकड़ पश्चिमी समुद्र पर जमती है।

panels.shot: medium two-shot of Rudrasimha III fading, Chandragupta II solid, against a backdrop of maps and coins
panels.action: Rudrasimha III appears semi-transparent, fading into shadow beside a firm, clear figure of Chandragupta II, behind them a ghostly map from Malwa to the sea overlaid with scattered silver coins.

dialogue.text: No inscription records the last day of Rudrasimha III, but the coinage tells us enough: a dynasty ended, a new order claimed its mints, and trade itself became a prize of empire.

i18n.hi: कोई शिलालेख रुद्रसिंह तृतीय के आख़िरी दिन को नहीं लिखता, पर सिक्के इतना बता देते हैं: एक वंश ढहा, नए शासकों ने टकसालें पकड़ लीं, और व्यापार खुद साम्राज्य की सबसे बड़ी लूट बन गया।

panels.shot: close-up of a hand stopping one die and raising another, symbolically
panels.action: In a symbolic scene, a strong hand presses down on an old Kshatrapa coin die, stilling it, while the other hand lifts a new Gupta die ready to strike, both silhouetted against a glowing forge.

dialogue.text: When the Gupta emperor took the satrap mints and copied their silver, he did more than conquer land; he captured trust, habit and the flow of wealth along the coast.

i18n.hi: जब गुप्त सम्राट ने क्षत्रपों की टकसालें लीं और उनकी चांदी की नक़्ल की, तो उसने ज़मीन से ज़्यादा जीता; उसने भरोसा, आदत और तट के साथ बहती दौलत की धारा पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of waves washing over a buried coin on the shore
panels.action: At the edge of the sea, a half-buried silver coin lies in wet sand as waves wash over it, distant ships sailing on the horizon under a soft evening light.

dialogue.text: An age can end without a final battle cry; sometimes it ends when a coin is struck for the last time—and another, in a new name, takes its place.

i18n.hi: हर युग को आख़िरी रणघोष नहीं मिलता; कभी‑कभी युग तब खत्म होता है जब आख़िरी सिक्का ढलता है—और उसी ठप्पे में, नए नाम वाला दूसरा आकर उसकी जगह ले लेता है।

title_i18n.hi: चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय ने क्षत्रपों का अंत किया

subtitle_i18n.en: When Silver Fell Silent: Chandragupta II and the Last of the Saka Satraps
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब चांदी खामोश हुई: चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय और आख़िरी शाक क्षत्रप
